description: `pick_next` has FOUR different signatures across the v3 spec, making the required-true PROPs untestable as a coherent contract. (1) REQ-M3 line 307: `menu.pick_next(menu, log_tail, history, now_ts)`; (2) Purity table line 21: `pick_next(menu, log_tail, history, blockers)` with `set[str]` typing; (3) PROP-P6-menu-pick line 63: `pick_next(menu, log_tail, history, blockers)`; (4) PROP-P7-pivot line 78: `pick_next(menu, blocked_set)` (2-arg). The cadence gate (FIND-2-005 fix) added to REQ-M3(ii) requires `now_ts` to compare `last_fired_ts + min_cadence_seconds <= now_ts`, but the Purity table signature has no `now_ts` parameter, so the pure function literally cannot perform the cadence comparison without reading a clock (= I/O leak into the pure layer, violating Purity Boundary). Either pick_next must take BOTH `blockers: set[str]` AND `now_ts: int` AND the signature must be identical in all 4 locations, or the cadence gate must be promoted to the I/O layer (e.g. lib/menu.py:execute_pick at line 51 already lives in the I/O column). Without one consistent signature, PROP-P6 / PROP-P7 / PROP-cadence / PROP-M3-pick-next are testing different contracts.
